name: Program Analysis
description: Static/dynamic analysis, symbolic execution, taint tracking, and bug detection for security.

uss.narrative:
The earliest papers in this set, from USENIX Security 2018, show program analysis maturing into a practical, security-driven discipline. A central thread is making heavyweight techniques scale to real bugs. QSYM: A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing (2018) is the anchor: it married concolic execution to fuzzing so the symbolic engine only solved the hard branches, turning a slow technique into a usable one. Alongside it, 2018 work pushed analysis into specific exploit domains: teEther (2018) automatically generated exploits for Ethereum smart contracts, NAVEX (2018) chained static and dynamic analysis to build exploits for dynamic web apps, and HeapHopper (2018) and Automatic Heap Layout Manipulation for Exploitation (2018) brought model checking and search to memory-allocator security. Meta-analysis appeared too, with Discovering Flaws in Security-Focused Static Analysis Tools for Android (2018) using systematic mutation to test the testers.

By 2019 the field broadened from "find any crash" toward semantic and domain-specific bugs and toward smarter fuzzing. Detecting Missing-Check Bugs (2019) and PeX (2019) inferred which security and permission checks a program ought to perform, catching logic flaws static tools had missed, while DEEPVSA (2019) and GRIMOIRE (2019) injected deep learning and structure synthesis into binary analysis and fuzzing respectively. A debloating sub-theme emerged as attack-surface reduction, with RAZOR (2019) and Less is More (2019) trimming unused code from binaries and web apps. This momentum carried into 2020, where data-flow-aware fuzzing matured in GREYONE (2020), firmware became analyzable via re-hosting in HALucinator (2020), fuzzer construction itself was automated by FuzzGen (2020), and analysis spread to privacy policies (PoliCheck, 2020), patch-based vulnerability signatures (MVP, 2020), and post-crash root-cause explanation (AURORA, 2020).

The most recent years show the area specializing and, increasingly, fusing learning with classical analysis. Smart-contract and blockchain security consolidated through TXSPECTOR (2020), SmarTest (2021), which guided symbolic execution with a language model, and EOSAFE (2021). Fuzzing kept refining its feedback signals, as in The Use of Likely Invariants as Feedback for Fuzzers (2021), while access-control reasoning scaled to cloud microservices in Automatic Policy Generation for Inter-Service Access Control (2021). By 2023-2024 the center of gravity tilts toward learned representations of code: VulChecker (2023) localizes vulnerabilities via graph neural networks, and Code is not Natural Language (2024) builds semantics-oriented graph representations for binary similarity detection. The arc runs from making symbolic and dynamic analysis practical, through pushing it into new domains and toward semantic bugs, to today's hybrid of graph- and learning-based methods layered on top of program structure.

milestones.title: QSYM : A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing
milestones.note: made concolic execution practical by pairing it with fuzzing, defining the dominant hybrid-fuzzing paradigm

milestones.title: teEther: Gnawing at Ethereum to Automatically Exploit Smart Contracts
milestones.note: opened automated exploit generation for smart contracts, launching the blockchain program-analysis line

milestones.title: Detecting Missing-Check Bugs via Semantic- and Context-Aware Criticalness and Constraints Inferences
milestones.note: shifted detection from crashes to inferred semantic bugs by learning which security checks code should perform

milestones.title: GREYONE: Data Flow Sensitive Fuzzing
milestones.note: showed lightweight data-flow/taint feedback could steer fuzzers to hard-to-reach code, advancing fuzzing's core signal

milestones.title: HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation
milestones.note: made embedded firmware broadly analyzable through abstraction-layer re-hosting, extending analysis to a hard new domain

milestones.title: SmarTest: Effectively Hunting Vulnerable Transaction Sequences in Smart Contracts through Language Model-Guided Symbolic Execution
milestones.note: fused language-model guidance with symbolic execution, an early bridge between learning and classical analysis

milestones.title: VulChecker: Graph-based Vulnerability Localization in Source Code
milestones.note: marked the turn to graph-neural vulnerability localization that pinpoints, not just flags, bugs

milestones.title: Code is not Natural Language: Unlock the Power of Semantics-Oriented Graph Representation for Binary Code Similarity Detection
milestones.note: represents the current state: semantics-oriented graph representations of code over naive NLP-style modeling

top4.narrative:
In 2018 the field split its attention between two fast-moving frontiers. One was the brand-new world of Ethereum smart contracts, where a single deployed bug could freeze real money: Securify: Practical Security Analysis of Smart Contracts (CCS 2018) and ZEUS: Analyzing Safety of Smart Contracts (NDSS 2018) brought static and formal analysis to bytecode, while teEther: Gnawing at Ethereum to Automatically Exploit Smart Contracts (USENIX 2018) showed analysis could go all the way to generating working exploits. The other frontier was making heavyweight symbolic reasoning practical for real bug-finding, exemplified by QSYM : A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing (USENIX 2018), which re-engineered concolic execution to keep pace with a fuzzer. Alongside these, taint and data-flow techniques pushed into new domains, as in Sensitive Information Tracking in Commodity IoT (USENIX 2018) and NAVEX: Precise and Scalable Exploit Generation for Dynamic Web Applications (USENIX 2018).

The next two years were defined by the marriage of fuzzing and program analysis, and by the quiet arrival of machine learning into binary understanding. Hybrid testing matured rapidly: Send Hardest Problems My Way: Probabilistic Path Prioritization for Hybrid Fuzzing (NDSS 2019), SAVIOR: Towards Bug-Driven Hybrid Testing (S&P 2020), and GREYONE: Data Flow Sensitive Fuzzing (USENIX 2020) all used analysis to steer fuzzers toward the code that matters, while RetroWrite: Statically Instrumenting COTS Binaries for Fuzzing and Sanitization (S&P 2020) and FuzzGen: Automatic Fuzzer Generation (USENIX 2020) attacked the practical barriers of instrumenting binaries and building harnesses. In parallel, Asm2Vec: Boosting Static Representation Robustness for Binary Clone Search (S&P 2019) and DeepBinDiff (NDSS 2020) showed that learned representations could make binary similarity robust to obfuscation and optimization. The community also turned a critical eye on its own foundations through SoK: Sanitizing for Security (S&P 2019) and core precision problems like indirect-call resolution in Where Does It Go? Refining Indirect-Call Targets with Multi-Layer Type Analysis (CCS 2019).

By the early 2020s the area broadened into firmware, embedded, and forensic settings while smart-contract analysis grew more rigorous. HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation (USENIX 2020) and Karonte: Detecting Insecure Multi-binary Interactions in Embedded Firmware (S&P 2020) brought analysis to devices that resist normal instrumentation, and Combating Dependence Explosion in Forensic Analysis (S&P 2020) tackled the scalability of taint-style provenance tracking for APT investigations. Smart-contract work moved from pattern detection toward soundness and verification, with VerX: Safety Verification of Smart Contracts (S&P 2020), eThor: Practical and Provably Sound Static Analysis (CCS 2020), and SAILFISH: Vetting Smart Contract State-Inconsistency Bugs in Seconds (S&P 2022). Spectector: Principled Detection of Speculative Information Flows (S&P 2020) extended information-flow reasoning to microarchitectural Spectre leaks.

Most recently the field has begun absorbing large language models, both as a tool and as an object of skepticism. PalmTree: Learning an Assembly Language Model for Instruction Embedding (CCS 2021) signaled the shift toward pretrained models for code, and BEACON: Directed Grey-Box Fuzzing with Provable Path Pruning (S&P 2022) continued sharpening directed analysis. Examining Zero-Shot Vulnerability Repair with Large Language Models (S&P 2023) asked whether LLMs could fix security bugs, and LLMs Cannot Reliably Identify and Reason About Security Vulnerabilities (Yet?) (S&P 2024) supplied the sobering counterweight, building benchmarks that show current models are not yet dependable vulnerability reasoners. The trajectory across these venues runs from hand-built static and symbolic analyzers, through analysis-guided fuzzing and learned binary representations, to a present where the open question is how much of bug detection can be entrusted to learning-based models.

milestones.title: QSYM : A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing
milestones.note: made concolic execution fast enough to pair with fuzzing, launching the hybrid-fuzzing era

milestones.title: Securify: Practical Security Analysis of Smart Contracts
milestones.note: brought scalable, semantic static analysis to Ethereum bytecode and opened the smart-contract analysis subfield

milestones.title: Asm2Vec: Boosting Static Representation Robustness for Binary Clone Search against Code Obfuscation and Compiler Optimization
milestones.note: introduced learned binary representations robust to obfuscation, seeding the ML-for-binary-analysis line

milestones.title: GREYONE: Data Flow Sensitive Fuzzing
milestones.note: showed lightweight data-flow/taint analysis could decisively guide fuzzers to hard-to-reach bugs

milestones.title: Spectector: Principled Detection of Speculative Information Flows
milestones.note: extended principled information-flow analysis to detect Spectre-style speculative leaks

milestones.title: Karonte: Detecting Insecure Multi-binary Interactions in Embedded Firmware
milestones.note: pushed static taint analysis into embedded firmware and cross-binary interaction bugs

milestones.title: Examining Zero-Shot Vulnerability Repair with Large Language Models
milestones.note: first serious test of LLMs as automated security-bug repair tools, marking the LLM turn

milestones.title: LLMs Cannot Reliably Identify and Reason About Security Vulnerabilities (Yet?): A Comprehensive Evaluation, Framework, and Benchmarks
milestones.note: provided benchmarks tempering LLM hype by showing they cannot yet reliably reason about vulnerabilities
